The win: make the n=2048 reduction MULTI-CTA / cooperative so 8 matrices fill 148 SMs. Fork the best (ce4c5eb9, all low-rank wins) + pull brief-4's accurate bulge kernels (bulge_tridiag_k, 2D-grid bulge_backtransform_k, dense→band bug fix, band-aware latrd_band, precision _bt_mm, AQ gate) from da74c94c4. Then de-serialize the chase for the b=8 case: (a) warp-shuffle the per-step reductions + warp-per-matrix to cut the 7-barrier-per-step count; (b) multi-CTA-per-matrix pipelined bulge front (cg::this_grid, NOT cudaStream — 'stream' is banned) so ~18 CTAs cooperate per matrix; (c) or WY-block the chase reflectors into tensor-core GEMMs. dense→band trailing update in TF32/fp16 (brief-4 confirmed gate-safe). Route ONLY n=2048 to this; per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Budget: reduction + banked 3ms bisect + fp16 back-transform + 1 NS < 186323us. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 44358 + 39/39 idle-verified. Distinct from brief-7 (low-rank n=512/1024) and brief-8 (nearrank peel).

trial 4 (measured, REVERTED - regression): reverse-WAVEFRONT cooperative back-transform (bulge_backtransform_coop_k, deterministic c*maxk+k slots, grid.sync per reverse tick). WHAT I BUILT + MEASURED (idle, GPU-exclusive; each trial committed+logged):
1. COMBINE base (trial 1): grafted brief-4's bulge two-stage onto the best branch, routed ONLY n=2048. Reproduced brief-4 exactly: n2048 b8 = 1876916us (~10x cuSOLVER 186323), geomean 52995 (regression). Correct starting point.
2. COOPERATIVE WAVEFRONT reduction (trial 2, the brief's core ask -- DELIVERED): new bulge_tridiag_coop_k. Exploits the diagonal-wavefront parallelism of bulge chasing -- sweep c and c+1 run concurrently once staggered S ticks (disjoint band windows), ONE CTA per in-flight sweep, cg::this_grid().sync() per tick, band in GLOBAL memory. BIT-EXACT vs the sequential chase (d/e err 0.0 at ALL n incl n2048 b8), eig_err~4e-5 vs eigvalsh. This DE-SERIALIZED the reduction: bulge_tridiag_k 1119ms -> bulge_tridiag_coop_k 148ms (7.3x), n2048 full 1876916->896561us (2.1x). Fills the GPU (~344-576 CTAs at b8 vs 8 before).
3. Barrier-free back-transform (trial 3), NS 2->1 (trial 6), BT CTA-width sweep (trial 7), window +-2nb->+-nb + tighter stagger S=P+3 (trial 8, ~33% fewer reduction syncs): stacked shape5 down to 781456us (2.4x total vs the serial bulge). geomean 49511.
4. FAILED de-serialization attempts (measured, reverted): (a) reverse-WAVEFRONT cooperative back-transform (trial 4) -- accurate but 4x WORSE (3474166us): Tmax~12270 grid.syncs dwarf the thin per-tick work when each active lane loops all n columns. (b) coarsened reduction P>1 (trial 5): P=5 WORSE than P=1 -- the reduction is NOT grid.sync-bound; halving concurrency (wider stagger) hurts more than fewer syncs help. P>=10 breaks correctness (dynamic lane->sweep remap violates window disjointness).

DECISIVE VERDICT (trial 9, direct floor measurement): with the bulge back-transform made a FREE no-op, the NON-back-transform floor for n2048 b8 = 395672us = 2.1x cuSOLVER's 186323us. Breakdown (per rep): coop reduction ~110-148ms (grid.sync-bound, ~12270/S syncs) + dense->band qr/tf32-GEMMs ~30ms + FP32 NS/Rayleigh SIMT ~27ms + bisect 11ms + twisted 5ms + ~50ms torch elementwise overhead (dense->band Python panel loop + gathers). So the bulge two-stage CANNOT beat cuSOLVER at b=8 EVEN WITH a perfect/free back-transform -- routing n=2048 regresses the geomean (best-case ~45700 > 44358). I kept the non-regressing floor (route empty). The scheduling win the brief targeted IS real (7.3x reduction de-serialization, GPU filled) -- but the two-stage's total work is intrinsically ~2x cuSOLVER's fused syevd on 8 SMs.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not exhausted; manager to weigh -- all require cracking MULTIPLE floor components simultaneously since any single one leaves the floor > cuSOLVER):
1. The back-transform (~386-438ms, 51-58%) is per-column-latency-bound: only n*b=16384 independent columns => ~3.5 warps/SM, and a long per-column reflector chain (ns=262656 tiny nb=8 reflectors). CTA-width tuning barely moved it. The lever is WY-GEMM blocking of the chase reflectors into tensor-core GEMMs (brief option c) -- unbuilt (the bulge reflectors are staggered/banded, so a clean panel WY needs a banded-GEMM; non-trivial). Even so, floor says this alone won't beat cuSOLVER.
2. The coop reduction's ~110-148ms is grid.sync-bound (~12270/S syncs at ~12us each for ~344 CTAs). Coarsening (P) failed. A larger-work-per-sync tiling that keeps concurrency (e.g. stripe-per-CTA handoff with coarse syncs, or a persistent-CTA design) is unbuilt.
3. The ~50ms torch elementwise overhead is the dense->band Python  panel loop + per-panel symmetrize/gather -- fusible into one kernel.
4. Larger dense->band bandwidth (nb=16/32) was measured WORSE for the coop path (concurrency loss) but ONLY tested with the current structure; a wide-band dense->band (cheap tensor-core O(n^3)) + narrow-window coop chase with restored concurrency is a different design point.
5. n=2048 is 1/13 of the geomean; the measured floor (2.1x cuSOLVER) makes it the structurally-hardest full-rank shape. If the manager wants to keep pushing n=2048, directions 1+2+3 must ALL land to get the floor under 186ms. Otherwise the non-regressing route-empty (this HEAD) is the safe combine contribution, and the reusable bulge_tridiag_coop_k (bit-exact, 7.3x) is available for any future band->tridiag need at small batch.
